user_needs.description: User shall be able to track their daily mood over time to monitor emotional patterns.
User shall receive evidence-based CBT therapeutic exercises including thought challenging, cognitive distortion identification, and alternative thought generation.
User shall be able to journal about gratitude as part of a structured therapeutic program.
User shall receive guided sleep hygiene content delivered in a progressive daily sequence.
User shall be connected to crisis resources immediately when expressing distress or suicidal ideation.
User shall be able to view their progress and therapeutic engagement over time.
User shall receive timely reminders to engage with therapeutic content.
User shall have their clinical information securely and accurately communicated to their care provider when a therapist handoff is initiated.
User shall be able to interact with the chatbot using natural language and receive contextually appropriate therapeutic responses.
User shall be able to save and retrieve therapeutic work completed during sessions, including thought records and journal entries.

product_requirements.description: The system shall allow the user to submit one mood check-in per calendar day, recording a mood score on a 1-10 scale.
The system shall store all mood check-in data and persist it across app sessions, updates, and backgrounding.

The CBT thought challenging module shall guide the user through all required steps in sequence: identify situation, identify automatic thought, identify cognitive distortion, challenge thought, and generate alternative thought.
The system shall save the full text of all user entries in therapeutic exercises, including thought records, without truncation or data loss.

The crisis detection algorithm shall identify crisis-related language regardless of capitalization, punctuation, misspelling, or formatting variations, and initiate the crisis escalation protocol within 2 seconds of detection.
The crisis escalation flow shall display current, verified crisis resource contact information including hotline numbers and text lines.
The sleep hygiene program shall deliver content in the correct sequential order (Day 1 through Day 14) based on the user's enrollment date.
The progress dashboard shall load and display the user's historical data within 3 seconds.
The therapist handoff workflow shall transmit only the correct patient's session summary and clinical data to the designated care provider. No cross-patient data leakage shall occur.
Push notifications shall render correctly on all supported OS versions, displaying formatted text as intended without exposing raw markup.
The chatbot shall gracefully handle unexpected user inputs, including emoji-only responses, empty messages, and nonsensical text, without entering infinite loops or requiring a force close.
The sentiment analysis model shall accurately classify user emotional state, accounting for common linguistic patterns including sarcasm, minimization, and indirect expression of distress.
The gratitude journaling feature shall prompt the user to save or discard an entry before navigating away from an in-progress entry on all supported platforms.
The app shall launch successfully and be fully functional regardless of the duration since the user's last session.

The system shall enforce that only features included in the current released product version are accessible to end users. Unreleased or deprecated features shall not be accessible through any user-facing pathway.

clinical_safety_criteria.description: Criteria for determining whether a bug has potential for clinical harm in a mental health digital therapeutic. A bug is considered to have clinical safety implications if ANY of the following are true.

criteria.description: The bug could prevent a user in crisis from receiving appropriate crisis resources or escalation to a human provider.

The bug could result in the chatbot providing a clinically inappropriate therapeutic response, such as reinforcing negative thought patterns, misidentifying emotional state, or skipping required therapeutic steps.
examples: Sentiment misclassification leading to wrong response
Providing positive reinforcement when user is distressed

criteria.description: The bug could result in protected health information (PHI) being disclosed to unauthorized parties or associated with the wrong patient.
examples: Session data sent to wrong provider
PHI visible in logs or notifications

criteria.description: The bug could cause a user to lose access to the therapeutic tool entirely during a period when they rely on it for mental health support.
The bug could undermine therapeutic efficacy by delivering incorrect content sequencing, skipping therapeutic components, or corrupting the user's therapeutic data or progress history.
examples: Wrong content delivered in a program sequence
Loss of journal entries or thought records
Incorrect progress data affecting clinical decisions

clinical_safety_criteria.note: When in doubt, flag as potential clinical safety concern. It is better to over-flag and have a human reviewer dismiss a false positive than to miss a genuine safety issue.
